gate_refusal: No VALIDATION.json is written for E34 (coordinator's decision, 2026-11-01). E34 is a rho-against-rho measurement with no index-calculus arm: there is no measured S in this unit for the gate's gae_band 'ic' slot. E18's psi arm, whose distances the result corrects, is linear algebra only with a modelled handover (note §9.3), not a measured end-to-end S. Putting a rho walk in the 'ic' slot would pass the gate by relabelling. Same reason as E29 (research/e29_twists_20261030/validator-report.json, gate_refusal). This report and the replay certificate stand on their own as evidence that E34's records and figures are what they say.

rho_reference_finding.statement: The strongest walk implemented on E18's eight j = 0 curves, pooled, at each weight of the band: the mul-lean cheap order-24 walk at 0 GAE and the op-lean cheap order-24 walk at 0.1 and 1 GAE, in each arithmetic; the cheapest arithmetic is Karatsuba at every weight (pooled cost per sqrt(n) 26.904, 97.956, 724.552 at 0, 0.1, 1 GAE). Against E29's order-6 walk, the walk E18's psi rows were measured against: 1.632 / 1.254 / 1.126 (schoolbook), 1.627 / 1.232 / 1.122 (Karatsuba).
rho_reference_finding.band_ranking: The op-lean cheap order-24 walk is ranked above both order-6 walks across the band, pooled, in both arithmetics (point estimates). The mul-lean walk is not ranked across the band against either order-6 walk (E29 order 6 / mul-lean 1.632 / 1.120 / 0.948 schoolbook; cheap order 6 / mul-lean 1.572 / 1.042 / 0.864): it supplies the 0 GAE factor as the cheaper implementation of the same walk (identical steps and digests). Against the band-ranked op-lean walk alone the 0 GAE factor is 1.563 (schoolbook) / 1.544 (Karatsuba), a handover shift of 2.58 / 2.51 bits instead of 2.83 / 2.81.

heuristic_validation_checks.check: null control for the statistical signal
heuristic_validation_checks.result: The deciding quantity is a ratio of walk costs, dominated by step counts of 16 walks per curve and arm. Null: the rho heuristic sqrt(pi n / (2 m)) for class size m. Observed order 6 at 0.924 and order 24 at 1.086 of the heuristic (mean over curves); pooled steps ratio 1.701 against the heuristic's 2.000. Per-curve steps-ratio standard errors are 13-21 %, so the per-curve ranks (3 of 8 against the cheap order-6 walk) are within sampling noise. The pooled cheap / cheap ratio at 1 GAE, 1.026 +- 0.067 (schoolbook) and 1.021 +- 0.066 (Karatsuba), is 0.4 and 0.3 standard errors from 1: the registered point-estimate rule ranks it, but the measurement does not resolve it statistically. Under the heuristic's step counts the ratio would be 1.772 / 1.373 / 1.207, so the shortfall comes from the observed pooled steps ratio, 1.701 +- 0.111, which is 2.7 standard errors below 2 (E29 registered [1.7, 2.3] for it, G2.105). What should happen as the parameter grows: the representative's per-step cost is independent of n and the heuristic steps ratio is constant, so the ratios should not trend with n; the per-curve steps ratio (1.29-2.10) shows no monotone trend in n over p = 241-1069.
not applicable (direct walks on the curves, no substitute sampler)

p = 241-1069, n = 2^31.7-2^40.2, 8 curves x 16 walks x 5 arms x 2 arithmetics; the representative costs are size-independent, but the ranking at 1 GAE rests on the measured steps ratio of these 8 curves (assumption: it does not drift with n)

cost_model_checks.result: F_p multiplications (F_p4 products at 19 schoolbook / 13 Karatsuba), the walk's set-up (32 jump points, start point) and the cheap arms' per-walk constants (40 or 42 F_p multiplications, 12 mod-n operations) included, the [d]G = Q check excluded; native operations cmp, neg, modn, hash, table each one count, priced at w * 97 F_p multiplications

every native operation is priced alike (a 40-bit mod-n multiplication and an F_p comparison both count one); GAE 97 (schoolbook affine addition) is used for the Karatsuba arm too, with 79 as a sensitivity; the walk stores every visited point (no distinguished points) and no batching of inversions across walks is implemented for these j = 0 walks (E27's batched arithmetic would lower rho further)

not reported by the producer. The walks store every visited class representative, so memory is proportional to steps: the order-24 walk stores 1.70x fewer points (pooled). Not a cost claim of E34; noted as a limitation

cost_model_checks.check: per-attempt cost x inverse success probability
cost_model_checks.result: every walk is run to its collision and every one of the 1,280 (and 16 control) walks succeeds (correct = true, recovered log 271 on every curve), so the measured mean cost per walk is the expected cost; no success-probability scaling applies

observations: The planted logarithm is 271 on all eight curves (E29's instances); the walks start from random combinations aG + bQ, so its size does not help them.

The counters obey identities derived from the counting rule on all 1,280 walks: table = 2 steps - escapes - 1, hash = 2 (steps - escapes - 1), mod-n outside the representative = 2 + 4 (steps - escapes - 1) + 5 escapes + 4 (+ 12 set-up on the cheap arms); every cmp and neg is the representative's.

The omitted-candidate control mismatches exactly members / 12 = 416 per curve: in a class of 24 members with twelve distinct abscissae the omitted candidate (3, 2) is the winner for exactly two members (+-), so the control is caught at its analytic rate.

Every n is prime and n = 1 mod 24 (validator's own Miller-Rabin), so an order-24 multiplier group exists; the order-24 action itself rests on E29's kill-test records (order_lambda_p = 24, group_order = 24) and E29's validator's own group computation (research/e29_twists_20261030/validator-report.json, K.2).

E34's code commit touches only examples/e34_cheap_rep.rs, src/cryptanalysis/mod.rs and src/cryptanalysis/twist24_rep.rs; E29's functions are untouched by it. Since then twist24_rep.rs changed by one behaviour-identical clippy line and quartic_folds.rs gained E33's pipeline-report fields; neither is in the replayed binary (built from bd0118f39).
limitations: Operation counts only; local container, not isolab-eks (unreachable). No wall time is claimed or compared.
The build target was on tmpfs, not the briefed shared target (disk); the build is still a fresh, independent build from a clean export of the recorded commit.

The producer's in-crate unit tests (twist24_rep::tests) were not re-run: the release test build needs about 9 GB of disk, which this container does not have; the replay of every record stands in for them.
The x = 0 identity case has no point on these curves (b0 t^3 is not a square), so it is untested by points, as §9.39 says.

Per-curve ranks and the 1 GAE pooled margin over the cheap order-6 walk are within the sampling error of 16 walks per curve and arm (see heuristic_validation_checks); the registered ranking rule uses point estimates.
The order-24 group order itself is not recomputed here from curve coefficients (they are not in E34's records); it rests on E29's kill test and its validator.
A CI job may move data files to the artifact store after push (it moved E34's PNGs); every replayed file is pinned by SHA-256 in the certificate.
